summary: Deschutes NF lookout near Sisters, Oregon: a 40-foot L-4 pole tower built 1932-33, pulled down in 1967 and gone by 1968.

facts.design: 40-foot round pole tower with a 14x14 L-4 hip-roofed cab
facts.status_note: Pulled down by a logging company in 1967; the register and firelookout.com list it as gone by 1968

staffing.status: lookout firemen recorded in 1936 and 1938, and a summer lookout job in 1961; no end-of-staffing date in these sources

events.note: Road and tower work began in October 1932; firelookout.com gives 1932 as the build year, and a history page says the tower was constructed in 1933
Paul Talonen placed on the butte as lookout fireman on August 5, 1936

A.D. Cleveland's summer job as a lookout on Abbot Butte, per an Albany Democrat-Herald item
Logging company pulled the tower down for the Forest Service; the first attempt failed and a leg was cut

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 1932 as the build year. The history page says road and tower work began in October 1932 and that the 40-foot tower was constructed in 1933. The record gives 1932 as the start and 1933 as completion.

sources.title: Abbot Butte
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (Oregon), Rex's Fire Lookout Page

notes_for_editor: No source describes what remains on the site today. The register has a 2002 photo captioned 'Site on June 3, 2002' whose content is not described. Access is omitted because no source gives it. The brief's 2010 FFLOS registration date (August 16, 2010) does not appear in the register text read, so it is not repeated. Searches surfaced a different Abbott Butte lookout in the Umpqua National Forest, Douglas County (spelled with two t's); it was excluded. The 1933 completion date comes from a history page and firelookout.com gives 1932, so the editor may want to choose one for the infobox.
